A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReferEverything, the REM framework and Ref-VPS benchmark. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison. Changed evaluation settings limit direct score comparisons, not identification of the revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original REM evaluations, backbone and decoder ablations, and qualitative analyses on established datasets and the newly collected Ref-VPS benchmark.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Wan and MeViS evaluations, annotation-agreement measurements, computational-cost measurements and extensive supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: v2 adds a principal REM variant using the Wan-14B diffusion transformer alongside the ModelScope model. Its joint spatiotemporal architecture uses single-stage fine-tuning instead of ModelScope's spatial-then-joint training. This substantially extends the implemented model family, while retaining the mask-latent objective, frozen VAE and single-pass decoding.

E1.justification: v2 adds training and evaluation on MeViS, substantially extending evaluation toward motion-dependent referring expressions. The earlier training sources and five evaluation benchmarks remain. Ref-VPS's additional clips retain the same 39 concepts and do not independently establish broader task coverage.

E2.justification: The new MeViS comparison includes VISA-13B, DsHmp and GLUS alongside Referformer. GLUS also joins the existing Ref-VPS comparison in v2 Table 4, whereas v1 Table 3 compared only MUTR, UNINEXT and VD-IT. The original in-domain and BURST/VSPW comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: Ref-VPS changes from 141 clips annotated at 24 FPS to 145 clips annotated at 6 FPS, with ambiguous pixels excluded using Ignore labels. The stated default evaluation resolution changes from original resolution to 512×512. v2 also introduces Wan and MeViS training schedules, controlled resolution/supervision experiments and temporal-consistency evaluation. These establish reported protocol changes without proving that every retained result was rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's backbone/CNN ablations, v2 adds latent-versus-pixel supervision, frozen-versus-tuned VAE and MLP-decoder comparisons; training-stage, data-ratio and noise ablations; annotation agreement and VAE reconstruction checks; quantitative failure, temporal-consistency and computational-cost analyses; and ambiguous-scene cases. Earlier backbone, fight-scene, failure-example and concept-coverage analyses are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Appendix B.3 newly specifies averaging inference measurements over 80 runs, and Appendix A.3 reports inter-annotator agreement. The timing repeats do not establish additional training runs. Neither version reports segmentation-performance seed variability, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds MeViS results of 53.5 and 60.3 J&F for ModelScope and Wan, respectively, plus Wan results and numerous diagnostic outcomes. Matched ModelScope entries change from 40.4 to 37.5 J on BURST and 49.56 to 49.0 on Ref-VPS; several baseline and backbone-ablation values also change. Revised protocols prevent interpreting these as same-setting regressions. Original Table 1 scores are retained with rounding.

T1.justification: Appendix B.7 adds a formal temporal-consistency metric in Equations (A)-(B), absent from v1. The original diffusion and segmentation Equations (1)-(7) remain substantively unchanged. The new signed IoU-difference definition permits cancellation, limiting its interpretation as temporal stability.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain preserving generative architectures for open-world referring segmentation and introducing Ref-VPS. v2 explicitly emphasizes benefits from advances in video generation in its abstract and conclusion, but v1 already articulated that relationship in Section 5.3 and discussed interchangeable backbones. The expanded experiments principally strengthen existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations connecting two-stage training to spatial priors, image/video balance to generalization, and VAE reconstruction to mask-domain compatibility. It discusses ambiguous ground truth, the limitations of temporal-consistency measurement and misleading consistency from empty predictions. Existing object-centric bias and fast-motion limitations remain in the appendix.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds Wan's 80k-step schedule, batch size and 17-frame clips, model-specific MeViS fine-tuning schedules, and inference-versus-scoring frame rates. Computational-cost sections document measurement hardware and baseline-estimation procedures. However, v1's exhaustive supervision inventory for the original baselines is omitted, and v2's general eight-GPU training statement is not clearly reconciled with its four-GPU ModelScope cost report.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting MeViS, Wan/DiT, GLUS, VISA, DsHmp, reconstruction analysis and annotation-quality evaluation. It extends comparisons to recent language-model-based video segmentation systems. The central positioning against object-centric RVOS and diffusion feature-extractor approaches remains; publication updates and merged duplicate citations are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, benchmark-collection narrative and discussion are extensively rewritten, and terminology changes from 'Referral' to 'Referring'. The appendix is reorganized into dataset, quantitative evaluation, qualitative evaluation and implementation sections. The existing generative-backbone analysis moves from the main text into the supplement.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 becomes a front-page teaser, and existing qualitative comparisons are extensively rearranged. v2 adds an annotation-pipeline diagram, ground-truth/Ignore visualizations and a quantitative failure plot, while expanding and regrouping tables for additional models, comparisons and analyses.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's limited decoder ablation and absence of annotation-agreement measurement, v2 adds controlled supervision/decoder experiments and independent annotation validation, substantially strengthening the central method and benchmark evidence. MeViS and Wan evaluations further test applicability. The flawed signed temporal-consistency definition and inconsistencies in training-cost reporting weaken those particular additions, but the stronger central validation provides a clear substantial net improvement. Revised Ref-VPS scores alone do not establish performance improvement.
